sentences.text: Naturally, there is even a row about smoky bacon crisps – an argument between the UK and EU about food labelling has become a classic of the genre.

sentences.text: It's a clash between those arguing it's worth swallowing some new rules to ease trade with the continent, or those whose message to Brussels is, "hands off our snacks" - even though we are not actually in the EU anymore.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Andy Burnham's big moment with the bloc top brass is fast approaching - the second annual EU-UK Summit since the UK's withdrawal from the EU takes place in Brussels on 20 November.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: That meeting is not supposed to be about whether the UK might one day go back in.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: The prime minister has suggested that is his long-term ambition - but is he really ready for what is to come?
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: First, Burnham inherited the broad deal that's likely to be signed.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: The UK and EU were originally meant to mint a new and, they hope, improved agreement back in May, then in July, and well, political upheavals mean one thing for getting things done – delay.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: But that means the outlines of a new agreement have been clear for many months, an approach based on "closer alignment" as Sir Keir Starmer proclaimed to us at the start of the year.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: So if the prime minister hails agreement, spare a thought for those who started the work to get it this far many months ago.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: One source familiar with the negotiations told me, "They are 90% there", with agreements designed to make life easier for food producers, a deal on emissions trading which could help manufacturers, and new arrangements for youth visas (although it's understood there is still haggling over putting a cap on the numbers).
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: An EU source close to the process said: "The bone of contention is a cap – we proposed 150,000, the UK proposed 50,000 – but we would expect to reach a compromise", even though it has been "very tense" on both sides.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: A last-minute call from the EU to cut tuition fees for its students is expected to be parked for now with more months of discussion to come.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Another fine tradition - agree what you can, but file some tough stuff away for future chat.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: There are dilemmas too on the EU's so-called "Made in Europe" plans – draft laws to protect its industries from being hammered by Chinese competition.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: The purpose is clear – to help the economy grow, with the prime minister quoting figures that suggest closer ties to the EU without going back in could add 0.4 percent to GDP.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: But as the tabloid-friendly row over salty snacks illustrates, making it easier to do business with the bloc doesn't come without a cost, and a political awkwardness.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Andy Burnham with Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission Talking to my colleague, the BBC's Business editor Simon Jack this week, the prime minister admitted the UK would have to follow more EU rules.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: "That's where we've ended up," Burnham acknowledged.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: And whatever your feelings on the matter, that lands us slap-bang back in the middle of the eternal dilemma of the relationship between the UK and the European Union.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: How much control is the UK willing to lose in the hope of bigger wins?
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Even when it comes to a relatively limited number of important issues that are on the table in the current discussions?
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: The prime minister has scrapped the limits of this troubled conversation, not just suggesting a closer relationship with the relatively dry and technical changes being discussed right now, but dangling the possibility of going back into the bloc one day.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Suggesting freedom of movement again, unlimited immigration for Brits who want to live or work on the continent and vice versa.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: That's after repeated promises, including from him, that that sometimes toxic debate would not be reopened.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: It seems the prime minister's main line of thinking is that with problems like long passport queues and red tape for business it is right and proper to try to sort them out.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: That is after all, what Rishi Sunak and then Sir Keir Starmer tried to do.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: But his willingness to contemplate going a lot further is based on a belief that the public's attitude has shifted – if you look at polling it does suggest that a majority of voters support going back into the EU , external .
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: It just so happens his own long-time conviction is to go back into the bloc one day.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: And that idea chimes not just with many Labour activists and members, but also with the Lib Dems, Greens and SNP – whose voters he'd be only too happy to peel off.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: But hang on, don't let Burnham's easy-breezy style mask that just casually mentioning he is open to us going back into the EU in the run up to this summit is a huge and difficult thing.
sentences.article_title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride

sentences.text: Whatever relationship he truly wants to seek, and even those involved in the conversations aren't quite sure he is even sure, don't expect a smooth ride from the EU.

sentences.text: In an interview you can see tomorrow, the EU's chief negotiator last time, Michel Barnier, told me the UK cannot pick and choose the relationship "à la carte".

sentences.text: If we wanted to go back in, he told me, the UK could forget the famous rebate, and there is no way to be in the huge trading bloc, the single market, without accepting freedom of movement.

sentences.text: One government figure told me, even now dealing with the EU there are "lots of very warm words, but quite a lot of arms folded".

sentences.text: An EU insider told me the mood has certainly changed.

sentences.text: Employees inspect the damage of a kindergarten in Kyiv following a Russian missile attack Overnight drone and ballistic missile attacks damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyhas said, causing blackouts and disrupting water supplies.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Zelensky said 12 Ukrainian regions came under attack with the capital Kyiv hit hardest.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Nine people are reported to have been hurt across the country, including one child, in the wave of attacks that consisted of more than 30 ballistic missiles and over 170 drones.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Zelensky wrote on Telegram , external that Moscow was preparing for the talks by launching attacks on Ukraine's "critical infrastructure".
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Temperatures are dropping in Ukraine, and parts of the country have had the first winter snow.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: "The situation in the capital is difficult, with disruptions to electricity, water, and heating supplies.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Residential buildings, the North Bridge, and a kindergarten have been damaged," Zelensky said.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: "In the Kyiv region, there were strikes on substations that connect the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine." In his latest update, Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the city's water supply system is back to operating normally.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: He also said around 60% of the city's apartment buildings were connected to the heating system.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: The energy minister, Denys Shmyhal, said there were power cuts in five regions but did not say how many homes were affected.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Debris and a broken window inside the kindergarten in Kyiv Zelensky added that beyond Kyiv, substations were damaged in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipro regions.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: The latest attacks come after US First Lady Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: She called for a "more enduring" ceasefire in Ukraine following a truce last week in the southern region of Kherson.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: She thanked both Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin, making no reference to the origins of the war, which began when Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, which has caused thousands of civilian casualties and the displacement of millions.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Hundreds of residents of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky facing starvation and constant bombardment were able to evacuate during a six-day ceasefire , which both Moscow and Kyiv credited Trump with brokering.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: "The lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace," she said.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Earlier this week, a number of people were killed when glide bombs hit an aid centre near Zaporizhzhia , with the death toll rising to 55 as teams search deeper into the ruins.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Zelensky added in his Telegram post on Saturday following the latest attacks that Ukraine was counting on increased bilateral support from the United States.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: He wrote: "We are counting on unity between both parties on issues of security, support for Ukraine, condemnation of Russian aggression, and increased sanctions pressure on Putin.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: "The resolve and consistency of the United States in supporting Ukraine are of great importance in bringing peace closer." Meanwhile, Zelenksy's spokesperson would not be drawn on reports that the Ukrainian president is to be invited to the UK for a state visit next year.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks

sentences.text: Monty and his dog, Ned, have been a fixture on the show TV horticulturalist Monty Don thanked viewers and his furry friend Ned the dog while presenting his final episode of Gardeners' World, after more than two decades on air.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: The head gardener on the long-running BBC TV series signed off from Longmeadow garden, where the show has been based for 16 years, on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: "From myself, Ned, and Longmeadow it's the final goodbye," he said on the programme, adding it had been "a privilege and pleasure" to share his garden experiences with so many people.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: During the episode, Don, 71, confirmed he would remain part of the presenting line-up for next year's Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Chelsea Flower Show.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Monty Don started on Gardeners' World in 2003, replacing Alan Titchmarsh He added he will feature in two winter specials, expected to air between now and Christmas.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: One celebratory episode will see him reflect on his years presenting the series and the changes he has seen at Longmeadow , external , which is also the garden of his private home, which he and his wife Sarah bought in 1991.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Don replaced Alan Titchmarsh on the show in 2003, at his predecessor's request.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: "I first began presenting Gardeners' World 23 years ago at Berryfields, and we came here to Longmeadow 16 years ago - in that time, things have changed," he recalled, on Friday's farewell.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: "The garden has grown, Nigel has been and gone, and Nellie and Patty [his previous dogs], but there has been one constant factor, and that has been the incredible privilege and pleasure of sharing my garden and my gardening life with you here, as well as working with so many superb people.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Thank you for coming on that journey with me and good luck with your own gardens in the future.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: So, for the last time... goodbye." Details of the next series of Gardeners' World will be announced at a later date, the BBC noted in a statement ahead of Don's farewell.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: His successor has not yet been named.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Bookmakers and viewers have pointed to regular co-presenters like Frances Tophill and Adam Frost as top contenders, though Tophill has played down expectations of stepping directly into his shoes.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Prior to fronting Gardeners' World, Don hosted other shows including Tomorrow's World, Holiday and - a preview of coming attractions - a gardening segment on This Morning.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: He took a three-year break from the programme after suffering a minor stroke in 2008.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: In September this year, Don announced that the current series would be his last.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: In a statement, he said working on the show had been a "deeply rewarding experience", but added that "now is the right time for a change".
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: The BBC said at the time that Don had "inspired and guided millions of viewers with his warmth, wisdom and passion for gardening" since joining the programme in 2003.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: Don was made an OBE by Queen Elizabeth, in 2018, for services to horticulture, broadcasting and charity.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: And he also received the RHS Victoria Medal of Honour - highest honour in horticulture.
sentences.article_title: Monty Don bids 'final goodbye' to Gardeners' World after two decades

sentences.text: This video can not be played What's it like to move to one of the UK's most remote islands?
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Katy Phenix's new life as a crofter on the UK's most remote inhabited island is a far cry from her previous life as a history teacher in a secondary school.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The 33-year-old relocated to Fair Isle from Redcar, North Yorkshire, with her partner Josh Moore, 35, and their children Teddy, 11, and Hetty, six, in July.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: They had never visited the island before moving there but were seeking more family time and a better quality of life.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Four months on, they say they have settled in to their "completely different" island life and feel "really lucky".
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Fair Isle lies half-way between Orkney and Shetland and has a population of about  60 people.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: It is three-miles (5km) long and owned by the National Trust for Scotland (NTS).
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Katy and Josh moved from Redcar to Fair Isle to start a new life Former secondary teacher Katy Phenix is now a part-time crofter Since moving to the island, Katy has begun working as a part-time crofter - a crofter is a person who shares pasture land to raise livestock.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: She said the family mainly moved to Fair Isle for more time together.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "We weren't living the lives we wanted," she said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "We were snatching time together over weekends and holidays.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "You get a mortgage, you get a car and you have to work to keep that up.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Moving to Fair Isle has cut all of that out." Fair Isle has a primary school and nursery, a local shop, post office and a community hall.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Katy has also taken up a post in early years education.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Her children are two of only five pupils at the local primary school.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Josh Moore's electrical skills have helped the island's energy project Josh is in high demand as a self-employed electrician because Fair Isle is off-grid with its own energy system.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The island's homes are powered by a combination of wind and solar power.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: A diesel generator provides a back-up supply.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Josh is working on a large battery replacement project.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "We're switching to new lithium ones," he said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "I'm also fixing people's lights and sockets." He said friends and family had been supportive of the family's move.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The pair are planning a Fair Isle wedding in 2027 The couple have been engaged for several years and are planning a wedding on the island in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "The church is literally next door", Katy said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The pair said they hoped another family with children would move to Fair Isle early next year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The National Trust for Scotland has advertised a further opportunity, with a five-bedroom house and 12-acre (5ha) croft available to rent.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: It is hoped a new family will move into this rented house on the island The trust said it was encouraging applicants with crofting and land management experience, trade skills such as plumbing or anyone looking to develop a craft  business on the island.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Angus Murray, NTS operations manager for Fair Isle, said: "We're inviting applications from hard-working and enthusiastic people who will bring skills, creativity and care to this special place." The deadline , external for applications is Sunday 8 November.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Fair Isle committee chairwoman Eileen Thomson says islanders have multiple jobs Eileen Thomson, who chairs the Fair Isle committee, said everyone had a role to play.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "You'll see people working in the fire service, the shop and the school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Eileen said the new tenants should be multi-skilled.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "A lot of the really big jobs need every single person to turn up and help, whether it's gathering all the common grazing sheep or doing the hay bales in summer," she added.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: She said creative people could also support the famous Fair Isle knitwear - a textile developed on the island in the early 19th Century.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: Katy and Josh brought seven pets with them Eleven-year-old Teddy hopes more children will move to the island so he can start a football team.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: "We do a lot of outdoor activity," he said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: His six-year-old sister Hetty added that their seven pets from North Yorkshire were "loving" island life. 'We moved to a remote island we'd never visited' National Trust for Scotland (NTS)
sentences.article_title: Secondary school teacher to crofter - life on the UK's most remote island

sentences.text: The computer game Worms (pictured) was created by Andy Davidson Andy Davidson was 22 when the game he programmed, partly in his last years at Bournemouth School, first hit the shelves.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Thirty-one years later, the various incarnations of Worms have sold enough copies that everyone in the UK could have one.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Davidson said: "Across all formats and all versions of the game it's up to 70 million now.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: I just can't get my head around it." Worms is a turn-based artillery game where players control a team of invertebrates who use a variety of creative ways to destroy their opponents.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Options included dynamite, homing missile, or exploding sheep.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Davidson said: "I chose worms because they hadn't been in a game before.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I thought I could get a lot of character into the animations because they're quite simple creatures." In fact, the game itself had very simple beginnings.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Bored during his A-levels, Davidson started programming an early incarnation of the game into his scientific calculator.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I found A-levels really hard, especially maths," he said.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "So I challenged my friend to make a game on a calculator.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: It was a little Casio graph-plotting calculator.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "And if you really pushed it hard you could get it to make a game.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: And so I made this little tank game.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: It snowballed from there." Worms: The game they tried to ban Listen as part of the Secret Dorset series Davidson's art teacher at the time was John Pakeman.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Pakeman was intrigued by what computers like Davidson's Amiga could do when it came to art.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "Once I saw what it was capable of I thought perhaps I better get one of these," he said.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "The game got banned from school," said Davidson.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "Everyone was crowding around the corner in the art room.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: That's when I thought I might be onto something." Even though he was there at the time, Pakeman was not sure of the potential impact of the game.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I wasn't sure if Andy created something, whether he could find a company that would take it on," said Pakeman.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I gather that's exactly what happened, he did find one, eventually.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I have never played the game.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: I think I've screenshots of it and I have friends who definitely have played the game.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "You mention Worms and they start beaming.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: My research tells me it's quite addictive." John Pakeman was Davidson's art teacher at the time Davidson signed with the West Yorkshire based company Team 17 to release Worms in November 1995.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: Its legacy is impressive - it was one of six British games celebrated on a special series of stamps in January 2020.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "When worms was on a stamp that's when it really hit home for my mum - she was  telling everybody it's been on a Royal Mail stamp." And Davidson's teenage voice still lives on in many people's mobile phones.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I did the voices of all the angry worms," he said.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: "I think 'Incoming' is the most famous one because people use it for text messages on their phones.
sentences.article_title: How computer game Worms went from classroom to classic

sentences.text: In my head it's still the little game I made for me and my friends." Explore fascinating stories from Dorset Listen and subscribe for the latest episode of Secret Dorset

sentences.text: Caroline Moore and Wendy Ireland say they were inspired by a poppy display on Southend Pier Novice crocheters have transformed a village church with a cascade of woollen memorial poppies.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: Caroline Moore and Wendy Ireland took up their crochet hooks last November with the aim of creating a display for their village of Friston in Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: The pair said they came up with the idea after "a few glasses of wine" after being inspired by a display on Southend Pier in Essex last November which they saw on social media.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: "Many hours of love and thought have gone into this," said Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: The display forms part of the village's Remembrance Day memorial "This has been a year in the making but this is our first time - so we're novices and we've only just learnt to crochet," she added.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: Moore said they decided to invite other people in the village which led to a group of women joining for a "knit and natter" over a cup of tea and cake.
sentences.article_title: Crochet novices create cascading poppy memorial

sentences.text: The exact number of poppies on the installation is being kept secret, so as not to spoil a competition for people to guess the total.

sentences.text: However, the pair said the amount meant they had slashed their poppy making time from an hour to just 20 minutes per poppy thanks to all the practice.

sentences.article_title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu

sentences.text: Skepta released The Fork and Knife on Friday, his first album since 2019's Ignorance Is Bliss One of the biggest names in grime is back - and he's picked his moment.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "Finally," Skepta promises BBC Newsbeat, "some good rap music, some good UK grime sounds." The Fork and Knife has been a long time in the making.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: Seven years on from his last album, Ignorance Is Bliss, and more than two years since it was first teased, the rapper knows how to keep fans waiting.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: But, as he's keen to point out, "you can't rush greatness".
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: And with a Mercury Prize, a Brit and two Ivor Novello Awards under his belt, greatness is no less than what fans expect from this titan of the rap scene.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: It's taken so long in part because Skepta's got big issues in his sights, with the new album taking on everything from immigration and racism, to Brexit and culture wars.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "Every time I write a lyric, it's important for me," he says.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: His 2009 track Reflecting, which charts his journey from a difficult childhood to becoming a successful musician, was a major turning point for him and grime, he says.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "I feel that was the first grime tune that was introspective and wasn't just about getting hype...
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "That was the first time I thought, 'OK, cool, this is a talent of mine'.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "I'm able to speak my true emotion with no filter, no chorus.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "I could just spit my emotions on a track that I made and people will feel it for years to come." Born and raised in Tottenham, north London, to Nigerian immigrant parents fleeing the country's civil war, Skepta, real name Joseph Olaitan Adenuga Jr, has long drawn on his early life in his music.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: Dipping into multiple genres for his sixth album, he's set out to explore what it means to exist between cultures and how it's shaped him as an artist.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: In Innocent Smile, his new track featuring Chase and Status and Madness frontman Suggs, he raps: "Ain't no love for an immigrant child / The writing's on the wall, has anyone else noticed? / Was it Brexit?
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: Was it Covid? / They point fingers, I feel hopeless." "I think grime is a product of immigration," he says, with some of the genre's biggest names and pioneers - like Wiley, Stormzy and Dizzee Rascal - all coming from similar backgrounds.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "That was important for me to represent what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "I'm British and I thought before I even get into a campaign, I wanted to let my stance be known that I'm for multiculturalism." And while Skepta's been focused on the message, he has also been deliberate about how he's delivering it.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "It took six years to make this because it's important to make sure we're not tone deaf," he says.
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: The image showed a group of men with shaved heads, one featuring a tattoo reading "Gas Me Up".
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: It had been a reference to skinhead culture, but Skepta acknowledged how without that context people could find it offensive and promised to be more mindful going forward.

sentences.text: Determined not to miss the mark this time around, he says: "I feel like we've delivered a classic." Early reviews are mixed as to whether critics agree, however.

sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: "And I'm here to set levels." In September, Digga D called out the viral 'UK Poo' trend, which saw a wave of tracks blowing up on TikTok defined by what he described as "foolishness".
sentences.article_title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'

sentences.text: The Speaker of the House of Commons has expressed "frustration" with the lack of progress on restoration to protect the Palace of Westminster.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Sir Lindsay Hoyle told the BBC the current process for approving essential renovations to Parliament amounted to "putting ourselves in handcuffs", and said more time was spent "doing surveys" than getting repairs under way.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for the ailing building's restoration, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: It said every additional year of delay cost taxpayers £420m, while its chairman warned the Palace could be left vulnerable to a devastating fire like that which engulfed the Notre Dame.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Sir Lindsay said his "biggest frustration" with the Victorian building's restoration was that "we're not getting on with the work".
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "We spend more time doing surveys," he told BBC Radio 4's The Week in Westminster .
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "Instead of doing surveys, why don't we start repairing the building?" The Speaker criticised current legislation which means the main renovations cannot begin until Parliament has approved the entire project's scope and funding.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "It's very frustrating when the Act of Parliament prevents you carrying out the major repairs that you need to.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "The major part and the most historic parts of the building haven't got it, and that's what we need." Asked about reports that Parliament might be given an opportunity to vote on the way forward before the end of 2026, Sir Lindsay said that was a matter for government business managers.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: "Who knows when it's going to come forward?
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Let's see what the House decides," he said.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Much of the 19th-Century building's network of wires and pipes dates back to the 1940s - and some to the Victorian era - according to a report , external which warned of an "impending crisis" a decade ago.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Fire safety issues and high levels of asbestos have also been identified.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: The BBC understands government whips have discussed holding a debate and vote by the new year, but no date has been scheduled.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: This would decide whether to proceed with up to £3bn of initial works and narrow down four current options, ahead of a final decision by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: One proposed option would see MPs and peers move out of the site for up to 24 years from 2032, costing up to £15.6bn.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: Another involves moving only the House of Lords out of the building, costing £39bn and taking 61 years.
sentences.article_title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker

sentences.text: The chairman of the body in charge of refurbishing Parliament defended the potential costs earlier this year , telling the BBC: "We're already spending £150m a year trying to keep the thing standing."

sentences.text: Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is £39,039.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Northumbria University's website said those graduates would be "repaying an amount less than the cost of a daily coffee" - a comparison that has been removed since the university was contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE website also only gives examples of monthly repayments for people earning up to £38,400 on other student loan plans, but does not include any real-world repayment examples for Plan 5 students.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Repayments are 9% of earnings over £25,000, so someone earning £30,000 will repay £37.50 per month, but someone earning £100,000 will repay £562.50 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan Russon, 21, is a recently graduated tax accountant from Cannock with a starting salary of around £29,000, meaning she will repay about £30 a month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: However, she expects to earn around £50,000 when she becomes chartered in three years' time, and will be repaying about £187 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan owes about £62,000 after graduating from the University of Birmingham with a degree in accounting and finance Megan says universities gave examples of repayments based on earnings of between £25,000 and £45,000 at open days and said graduates "wouldn't even notice the repayments because they should be minimal".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "At the time, I wasn't sure what salary I was even going to be on when I graduated," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The University of Exeter said Plan 5 loans were written off a decade earlier than they actually are, Royal Holloway and Edge Hill listed the wrong repayment thresholds, and Harper Adams said students from England were still on Plan 2 loans.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: All four universities have updated their websites since being contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "I'm pretty shocked at what the BBC has uncovered here and I'm going to be raising it with the relevant MPs and urging them to write to the universities in their constituencies to make them step up and do a better job," Dame Meg said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She said the DfE should be "taking the lead" by reflecting repayments for higher earners, but that universities also "have a responsibility to the young people that they're taking on board for the three or four years of their degree".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The naming of smoky bacon-flavoured crisps has become the latest political headache to emerge from the government's bid for closer ties with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The government is negotiating a deal on food standards in a bid to cut costs for British companies trading with Europe.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Labour ministers have been keen to talk up the potential economic benefits of the agreement, which could be announced at a summit later this month.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But the deal's requirement for Britain to adopt EU food rules in a wide range of areas has threatened to reignite sovereignty debates from the Brexit era.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Labour ministers have been keen to sidestep talking about the impact of alignment in particular sectors, instead stressing the overall economic boost it expects the food deal to bring.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: On Thursday, Environment Secretary Angela Eagle told a radio presenter he should "get a life" when he asked about the potential impact of the new rules on snacks, such as smoky bacon crisps.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But it highlights the political dangers for the government of realigning with regulations that British politicians have not been able to shape, with the Conservatives and Reform UK keen to pounce on cases showing Britain to be a "rule taker" from Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: It is not the first regulatory skirmish over smoky bacon crisps - following previous headlines over how the well-loved British flavour could be affected by an EU decision in 2024 to phase out a number of artificial smoke flavourings.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Now, the flavour name itself has been called into question by a separate EU attempt to restrict how descriptions of meat are used to market food.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Under rules adopted this summer, the EU plans to restrict the use of 31 terms, including bacon, drumstick and steak, to products that contain meat, claiming consumers could be confused by plant-based alternatives using the same names.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The European snack industry is seeking clarity on how the rules, which will also cover terms such as pork, chicken and beef, would apply to meat-flavoured crisps, including those flavoured without the use of any meat extracts.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The UK government has said it expects the new regulations to be in scope of its proposed food standards deal.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The new EU rules, which will not come into force until after August 2029, will allow the European Commission to create exemptions for meaty names with an established long-term use to describe other types of food product.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The Brussels-based body is yet to set out how it plans to use this power, or what it means for snacks.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: A group of conservative German MEPs are also seeking a specific carve-out for meat names in snacks and sauces in separate legislation , external currently making its way through the European Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The Food and Drink Federation, which represents British crispmakers including Walkers and KP Snacks, has been supportive of the government's bid to reach a food deal due to its potential to reduce trade barriers with Europe.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But it has highlighted the new rules as an example of where it wants the government to work with industry to ensure UK interests are reflected in EU decision making.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: "Meat protections are an example of a new EU rule that UK businesses will need to comply with, but which the UK was not involved in developing," added the body's chief scientific officer Kate Halliwell.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The Potato Processors' Association, which also represents a number of major snackmakers, said it was monitoring the situation closely and wanted to see clarification of how the rules could affect its members.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Vanessa Richardson, its deputy director general, said her association supported moves to reduce "unnecessary barriers" in the trade of food products.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But she added it was important that the government's deal is implemented in a way that "avoids unintended consequences for established product descriptions which consumers clearly understand as referring to a flavour".
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: High above the Arctic, powerful winds usually circle the North Pole each winter, helping trap some of the coldest air on Earth.

sentences.text: But this circulation, known as the polar vortex, has weakened and shifted position in recent days.

sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: However, as this is happening so early in the season, there are few historical examples to compare with and it could throw current winter forecasts into even more uncertainty.
sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: The polar vortex develops every autumn as temperatures fall in the Arctic.
sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: Strong westerly winds form in the stratosphere, roughly 10 to 30 miles (15-50km) above Earth's surface, locking the coldest air near the pole.
sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It is a true engineering marvel.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Engine-makers continually vie for access to the technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Rolls-Royce, GE and France's Safran are among the few firms that have perfected the process.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: In September, GE Aerospace announced , external it would acquire its turbine blade supplier for $11.75bn (£8.78bn).
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Neither company responded to BBC News' requests for comment but the move has been described as an effort to ensure supply of these critical components.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Separately, in March, Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham blade casting facility.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Turbine blade specialists continue to work on improving the capabilities of this little-known technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: All the while, China is desperate to prove that its engineers can produce turbine blades of the same quality as those in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Who will come out on top?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Demand for [turbine blades] is huge.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: So few companies have managed to do it, which does give it this kind of magical aura," says Bill Sweetman, an aviation industry writer and consultant.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: He suspects GE Aerospace's recent move is about securing reliability and predictability in the notoriously volatile aircraft manufacturing supply chain.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The casts play a crucial part in the cooling process But why is the single crystal casting process, which has been around for decades now, still so specialist?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: To grow one of these blades, asserts Fifoot, is to "fight the laws of the universe".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: This is because each molten blade would naturally cool into a solid object consisting of many small grains of metal alloy, all jumbled together.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But you don't want a crumbly sugar cube, you want a perfect diamond.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Getting a single crystal to grow into the shape of the blade instead isn't just a matter of cooling the molten version down slowly, the process also uses a bizarre trick called a pigtail.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Sometimes a blade doesn't cool quite as planned, for example two crystals form within it instead of just one, and the metal alloy must be reprocessed so that the manufacturer may re-use the material.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Special ceramic coatings also protect blades from extreme temperatures inside engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And another important feature is that blades are cast with tiny channels that allow a flow of cooler air to coat them in a kind of film while the aircraft engine is working.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "The drive at the moment [across the industry] is currently to make those cooling passages really intricate," says Paul Withey, at the University of Birmingham, who formerly worked for Rolls-Royce.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The more turbulent those little flows of cool air are, he explains, the more they will knock heat out of the surrounding, much hotter air.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And blade-makers also seek to reduce the mass of these components as much as possible.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "If we can take any weight out of it, you can run that engine more efficiently using less fuel – you can spin it faster and hotter," says Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Plus, Western manufacturers also have lengthy safety records under their belts.

sentences.text: China must compete on practically every aspect of aircraft manufacturing , external – by no means just on turbine blades – in order to make serious in-roads.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "You can definitely see that happening but it's a long, uphill struggle," adds Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Demand for aircraft is currently high, which is already straining various supply chains in the industry.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: That demand could grow higher still, suggests Withey.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the next few years, one of the two main aircraft manufacturers, Airbus and Boeing, could launch a new short-haul plane , external , he says.
