sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood says she'd like to still pick up the traditional PR skills her role isn't currently focused on, but is confident of her future in the agency's growing AI team.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There's certain things that I haven't had the chance to do yet, like directly pitching to the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: I absolutely plan to do this," she says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Graduates becoming too AI-centric is an issue for Simon Pratt, chief operating officer at Portman Finance Group.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He says being able to use AI effectively is important, but the company's two-year graduate programme is fully centred on "learning the trade".
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Our graduates rotate across four areas at six-month intervals, working directly alongside senior relationship managers to learn their trade," Northampton-based Pratt explains.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "They'll learn all of our financial products, how to draft credit papers for submission to lenders, and how to build meaningful relationships with our customers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: They'll progress to running transactions from start to finish." Claire Reid, PwC UK's chief technology and innovation officer, believes graduate roles that are too AI heavy won't necessarily provide graduates long-term career progression.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There will be no graduate job now that doesn't require a baseline of AI literacy," says Glasgow-based Reid.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "But AI skills on their own are not going to help you in your career.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: You've got to couple that with that sector knowledge of what that client actually wants." Back in Coventry, Dillan Patel is confident his AI work will continue to be valuable, and he wants to keep building on it.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I don't think I'd want to explore different positions within the business.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Through my involvement in AI-related projects, I already work closely with different areas of the business and I'm gaining valuable knowledge and experience along the way," he says.

sentences.text: Growing up in a council flat in the 1980s and 1990s, my mum would often point out homes that tenants had bought from the council.

sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: It was introduced in 1980, three years before I was born, when Margaret Thatcher's government gave council tenants in England the legal right to purchase their homes at a discounted price.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: Supporters welcomed the chance for working-class families to own their own home and build wealth.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: One bought an almost identical flat to ours in 1989 for £21,200, after receiving a discount of £18,800.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: More than 40 years after its introduction, Right to Buy remains a debate about political values as much as housing policy, balancing the home ownership ideal against the desire to preserve social housing for future generations.
sentences.article_title: Thatcher's Right to Buy created a generation of homeowners - did it also fuel the housing crisis?

sentences.text: The first public words from the prime minister after the American midterm elections were instantly revealing about contemporary international politics and diplomacy.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "Well, President Trump has accepted the results," Andy Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: It is not an observation British leaders have frequently had to make about recent American presidents - that they are not disputing the result of elections in their own country.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: But what would previously have been taken for granted no longer can be.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Burnham remains in the foothills of establishing a relationship with the president – so far it has amounted to a handful of phone calls and one face-to-face meeting at the United Nations in New York in September.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: As he continues to attempt to build a rapport with Donald Trump, he will be doing so with a president in a wildly different political situation than when Sir Keir Starmer was trying to build bridges with him.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: No longer is this a story of an extraordinary comeback, but of a midterm president seemingly punished for the consequences of a foreign war the type of which he had originally promised to avoid.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Time to focus on cost of living, says PM after US election results Trump's loss limits powers at home, but it will likely be different abroad And it is noticeable that the British government's public reaction is grounded too in the consequences of the war with Iran: the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all and that's the cost of living," the prime minister said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: And, bluntly, it is one that puts many, including many of America's allies, in alignment with many in America, Democrat and Republican, who when asked why these elections went as they did, point at the prices displayed outside any petrol station.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Speaking before the votes in America were counted, the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband reflected on this when I spoke to him on BBC Newscast , external .
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: When I asked him specifically if he feared that a domestically humiliated Trump may prove more belligerent internationally, it was to the Iran war the foreign secretary referred.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "We know that we need a diplomatic way out of this conflict, and so that is one of the things that we're working on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: It's something I talked to the US Secretary of State about at the G20, and it's something we continue to work on," he added.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: The foreign secretary met Marco Rubio at the meeting in Atlanta last week.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: But the big question for the British government, and so many others, is does defeat at home make it more likely that President Trump gets angrier abroad?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Or, do America's traditional allies, the UK, the European Union, Canada, Australia and others feel more strident and willing to work with Donald Trump's domestic political opponents to try to challenge and restrain a weakened president?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: The answers to these two final questions will determine much in world affairs in the next couple of years.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Cocaine-related deaths overtook heroin for the first time in 2015 The number of deaths from cocaine use in England and Wales has nearly quadrupled in a decade, overtaking those attributed to heroin for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Cocaine was linked to more than one in five drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025, more than any other single substance, with charities blaming its increased purity and availability.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Meanwhile a record 115 ketamine-linked deaths were registered, almost twice as many as in 2024, according to Office for National Statistics data , external .
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: The overall rate of drug deaths fell for the first time since 2012.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: But experts pointed out regional inequality was growing, with the rate of such deaths more than twice as high in the North East as in London.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: There were 5,519 drug poisoning deaths registered in 2025 in England and Wales, the equivalent of 92.4 deaths per million people.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Of these, cocaine was mentioned in 1,233 cases - slightly fewer than the previous year but higher than the 1,210 deaths linked to heroin or morphine, which also marked a fall from the previous year's level.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: However, deaths linked to opiate and opioid drugs combined were still higher.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: The ONS also said there was a lag between deaths occurring and being registered.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: The fatality rate fell from 93.9 deaths per million people a year earlier, representing the first annual decline since 2012.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: In September, National Records of Scotland said drug deaths there had risen by 11% in 2025 on the year before, marking the worst mortality rate in Europe, In May the Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency said drug-related deaths rose by 7.1% between 2021-23 and 2022-24 , external .
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Dr James Morgan, who specialises in addiction and mental health at London Metropolitan University, said while there had been a slight decrease in deaths "the numbers remain objectively high", with total drug fatalities in England and Wales roughly doubling since 2012.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "What we are seeing is increasing polarisation and growing inequalities, where the poorest regions are falling behind, and more affluent regions doing better," he said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: The steepest increases were found in formerly industrial areas with high levels of poverty and unemployment dating back to the 1980s, including the North East, Wales, Yorkshire and the Humber, the North West and the East Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Morgan pointed out that cocaine death figures included not only those who snorted the drug but also users who injected it or smoke crack cocaine in combination with opioids or counterfeit pharmaceutical drugs.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "The small decline in deaths related to cocaine should not be over-interpreted.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Most important is that deaths relating to cocaine remain roughly quadruple what they were in 2015 and are now more frequent than deaths relating to heroin or morphine," he said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Meanwhile, ketamine was referenced in 115 deaths last year - almost double the year before and up from just seven fatalities 10 years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Morgan said this was down to lower prices and use of the drug becoming normalised.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: He said there were increasing reports of young people becoming dependent on ketamine and suffering acute health difficulties such as bladder damage.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Anthony Irvin (pictured with sister Nyk) died from drug poisoning in 2025 Mike Trace, CEO of the addiction charity Forward Trust, said drug poisoning deaths remained high because of factors including the proliferation of very strong synthetic opioid drugs called nitazenes .
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "We know that increasingly potent drugs like nitazenes are making their way on to the market.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: We know that established drugs like cocaine are growing in purity which means they come with much higher risks to users," he said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Nitazenes can be many times more potent than heroin and have been linked to hundreds of UK deaths.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: Tom Powell and Nyk Irvin's brother Anthony Irvin died from drug poisoning in Ramsgate in September 2025 at the age of 52.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: His siblings believe his death was caused by a supply of drugs being contaminated with synthetic opioids, but say delays in blood testing mean they will never know for sure.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Today's figures are shocking," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: "We are fighting to wake people up to the scale of the problem."
sentences.article_title: Cocaine overtakes heroin as leading cause of drug deaths in England and Wales

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A positive result does not automatically mean there is cancer, and a negative result is not a guaranteed all-clear.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Health secretary Yvette Cooper said she hoped simple blood tests such as these would help identify patients needing urgent investigation much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Michelle Mitchell from Cancer Research UK said: "GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need." sentences.text: Two-year-old Finlay Roberts died after spending hours in a crowded hospital corridor.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner raised concerns about a lack of basic observations done by busy staff.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A new early warning system is being introduced in hospital emergency departments in England to help busy NHS staff identify sick children who are dangerously deteriorating.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A high overall score means a child needs more urgent attention.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Concerns from staff, parents, carers or the child themselves will trigger an immediate escalation of care.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: It comes after Health Secretary Yvette Cooper promised to stop "corridor care"  for sick children because of long waits for hospital beds.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The new National Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS) asks staff to check, log and grade vital signs, such as blood pressure, heart rate and oxygen levels.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The initiative is designed to save lives ahead of winter, when pressure on the NHS is at its highest.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: On the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper recently talked about the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts, who died in 2024 after spending hours in a hospital corridor before being discharged.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Cooper apologised to Finlay's parents on behalf of the NHS, saying: "No child should be treated in a corridor.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner raised concerns about a lack of basic observations done by busy staff , external .
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Martha Mills died aged 13 at King's College Hospital in London in 2021 A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: Duncan Burton, chief nursing officer for England, said the new early warning system for children in emergency departments was an "important next step in improving care for children and young people across England for this winter - and beyond".
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: He added: "In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child's condition is deteriorating.
sentences.article_title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E

sentences.text: "This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters." The early warning system for children, PEWS, is a collaboration between NHS England and the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health and the Royal College of Nursing.

sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves contain toxic compounds, while tough stalks and seeds may not be suitable for young children.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has ruled out reparations but is open to a formal apology The UK has signed up to "structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith" talks that address the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, Commonwealth leaders in Antigua have said.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: The formal conclusions marking the end of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, known as the communique, is the joint text setting out what has been agreed.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: The 18 page document , external includes a paragraph in which the leaders "welcome the agreement of the Government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms".
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham opened the door to a formal apology on behalf of the UK for its role in the slave trade, while ruling out the prospect of reparations.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: Officials said the timeframe for the talks would be agreed at a later date, though the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has suggested they are likely to conclude in around a year.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: This will be determined, sources said, in the "structured dialogue" the UK is promising with countries that have long demanded that the pain and lasting legacies of the slave trade are, as they see it, properly addressed.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: Burnham said his "new approach with the Commonwealth" had been "well received" at the summit.
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: He said it had "been the most successful meeting of the Commonwealth in recent times," adding that "the King's words have resonated powerfully here and we're really pleased with how it's gone".
sentences.article_title: UK commits to 'time-bound' talks on slavery apology

sentences.text: King Charles III, speaking in his role as Head of the Commonwealth, told the meeting: "The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other Members of our Commonwealth.

sentences.text: Patients in many parts of the country have been left unable to access their GP surgery online after a tech firm went into administration.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Silicon Practice ran digital services, including websites, online booking and consultations, for around 500 practices in England – just under 10% of the total.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Practices across the country, including in London, Gloucestershire and Norfolk , have reported problems.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Services in Wales are also affected.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: GP leaders said the problem would cause huge disruption, given the scale of online booking that now takes places.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Patients in areas that are affected are being advised they will have to make appointments via the phone.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Since last year , all practices in England have had to offer online appointment booking.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Currently, more than 40% of appointments are made that way.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: An NHS England spokesperson said while "the majority" of GP practice websites were running as normal, some using Silicon Practice will be affected.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: "If your GP practice website is unavailable and you need help, you should contact your practice by phone or in person as usual." Affected practices have been contacted by NHS England with advice on how to maintain business continuity and minimise the impact on patient care.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Silicon Practice ran the digital tool FootFall, which it advertised as reducing patient phone calls to practices by 30%, by working to "free your reception team from routine admin and manage demand more efficiently.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Proven in 1,000+ GP practices across the UK".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs, said: "GP practice websites are an increasingly important way for patients to access care, book appointments and find information about the services available to them.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: "When websites are not working, it can be hugely disruptive for patients and place additional pressures on already stretched practice teams.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Laura gave birth to her son Arthur in 2018 "Women, since the beginning of time, have birthed and looked after children and I just couldn't be bothered.

sentences.text: The NHS says postnatal depression , external , also known as postpartum depression, is a "common" mental health condition that can happen after having a baby.

sentences.text: "Postnatal depression can happen to anyone and this is why the veil of shame needs to come down, through education or through listening to people," said Laura.

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The world has been rapidly warming for around a century, causing weather patterns to change.

sentences.text: Since the 1980s, each decade has been warmer than the previous one, the Met Office says. 2024 was Earth's hottest year on record , with climate change mainly responsible for the high temperatures.

sentences.article_title: A really simple guide to climate change

sentences.text: Achieving "net zero" is the world's key strategy to fight climate change, which is already having serious consequences for people and nature around the globe.

sentences.text: The Confederation of African Football (Caf) will instead retain the tournament's traditional biennial staging, with its president Patrice Motsepe saying the U-turn was based on "advancing, protecting and promoting" the interests of the African game.

sentences.text: Yiech Pur Biel (left) is leading the first ever refugee team at the Youth Olympics When he started running, Yiech Pur Biel had to compete barefoot.

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: In 2016, Biel made history competing in the 800m event as part of the first Olympic refugee team at the Rio summer Olympics in Brazil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Ten years on, he's making history again leading the first refugee team for the Youth Olympics as their Chef de Mission.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Joining almost 3,000 athletes, the small team of six will be wanting to make sure their debut counts - but Biel says they're also hoping to send a message that "refugees still need our help".
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Hosted in Senegal, Saturday's opening ceremony will launch the first ever Olympic sporting event on African soil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Africa is home to nearly 45 million displaced people, out of almost 120 million globally, representing the world's biggest displacement crisis.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Oval Office.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The executive order declares the president's official office, which he has renovated, to be a national monument.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: "We're making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape," Trump told reporters on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The order does not prevent future presidents from changing the decor of the famous room.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The document says that it does not "restrict the President's authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's historic structure or architectural character".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: American presidents currently have the power to make some changes to the White House but large projects require the permission of Congress.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The order comes months after Trump tore down the entirety of the White House East Wing in a project that has faced legal challenges.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The project was not approved by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Construction has continued, with plans to turn the space into a new ballroom.

sentences.text: How Trump is remaking the White House in his own image Signing the new executive order on Thursday, the president said: "We like the Oval Office, and it's a symbol, like the White House itself.

sentences.text: It's a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country." He added that world leaders who have visited in recent months have complimented his decorative changes to the room.
